Test if parameter needs a vector

needs_vector.Rd

Runs a series of expectations with incorrect parameter values expecting errors. The values are selected to cover all different manners of incorrect input.

Usage

needs_vector(
  param,
  expr,
  ...,
  strict = FALSE,
  any_missing = TRUE,
  all_missing = TRUE,
  len = NULL,
  min_len = 0L,
  max_len = Inf,
  unique = FALSE,
  null_ok = FALSE
)

Arguments

param

character(1)
Name of the parameter to test.

expr

call(1)
Example call to the tested function that does not fail.

...

Reserved for future extensions and must be empty.

strict

logical(1)
Whether to disallow the vector to have additional attributes; if FALSE, allows e.g. factors and data frames.

any_missing

logical(1)
Whether missing values are allowed or not.

all_missing

logical(1)
Whether vectors with no non-missing values are allowed or not.

len

integer(1) | NULL
Exact length of the vector. If specified, can't specify min_len nor max_len.

min_len

integer(1)
Minimum length of the vector.

max_len

integer(1)
Maximum length of the vector. Must be more than min_len. If these were to be equal, set len instead.

unique

logical(1)
Whether all values must be unique or not.

null_ok

logical(1)
Whether NULL is also allowed or not.

Value

Nothing, called for its side effect of running expectations.

Details

Uses testthat::expect_snapshot() under the hood.

Examples

needs_vector(
  "subset.of",
  checkmate::test_names(letters[1:5], subset.of = letters),
  any_missing = FALSE,
  null_ok = TRUE
)
#> Error in loadNamespace(x): there is no package called ‘checkmate’
